about: Weeks 1-9 follow the NHS Couch to 5K plan exactly. Weeks 10-11 and the continuing weeks are this app's own proposal, not NHS content. Runs are Monday, Wednesday and Saturday, so there is always a rest or lifting day between runs. Edit any text or duration here; the app reads this file as-is.
effort: Easy and conversational: you should be able to speak in short sentences. Walking breaks are part of the plan, not a failure. Time on feet matters more than speed.

weeks.title: Couch to 5K, week 1
weeks.advance: Move on if all three runs were manageable. Repeating week 1 is common and fine.

weeks.title: Couch to 5K, week 2
weeks.advance: Move on if all three runs were manageable and nothing hurt in a way that changed how you moved.

weeks.title: Couch to 5K, week 3
weeks.advance: Move on if the 3 min runs felt controlled.

weeks.title: Couch to 5K, week 4
weeks.advance: Week 5 has bigger jumps. Move on only if the 5 min runs felt steady.

weeks.title: Couch to 5K, week 5

runs.note: The biggest jump in the plan. Slow down as much as you need to. If you have to walk, that's fine. Repeat run 2 or this week if it was too much.

weeks.advance: Move on if you finished the 20 min run, even slowly. If you had to stop, repeat week 5.

weeks.title: Couch to 5K, week 6
weeks.advance: Move on if the 25 min run was completed at an easy pace.

weeks.title: Couch to 5K, week 7
weeks.advance: Move on if all three 25 min runs felt sustainable.

weeks.title: Couch to 5K, week 8
weeks.advance: Move on if all three 28 min runs felt sustainable.

weeks.title: Couch to 5K, week 9

runs.note: Thirty minutes of running is not the same as 5K. At an easy pace, 30 minutes is usually about 3.5 to 4.5 km. The next weeks build from here.

weeks.advance: Move on once all three 30 min runs are done without pain. This completes the NHS plan.

weeks.title: After Couch to 5K: consolidate

runs.note: Repeat the week 9 run. Keep it conversational.
Steady means comfortably hard: you can say a few words, not full sentences. This is roughly the effort of a sub-35 5K. Do not sprint.
About 10% longer than your longest recent run, and no more. A single run much longer than recent ones is linked with higher injury risk.

weeks.advance: Move on if all three runs were pain-free and the 33 min run stayed conversational.

weeks.title: 5K check week

steps: Then 4 × 20 sec relaxed quicker running, walk back between
5 min easy jog after the walk
Run 5K at a steady, even effort
runs.note: Only if weeks 9 and 10 were pain-free. A sub-35 finish needs faster than 7:00 per km (about 11:16 per mile). Start a little slower than that and speed up after 3 km if you can. If you're not ready, run 33 min easy instead and do the check in a later week. Missing 35:00 now doesn't mean the goal is off.
Only extend if the 33 min run felt easy. Otherwise repeat 33 min.

weeks.advance: Continue to the ongoing weeks. If you haven't done the 5K check yet, it stays available on the middle run.

weeks.title: Ongoing: build toward a comfortable 5K

runs.note: Steady = comfortably hard, roughly 5K-goal effort. Once a month, you can replace this with a 5K check if you've been pain-free.

steps: Run easy for the longest duration you've comfortably done, plus up to 3 min
runs.summary: Long easy run, +3 min at most
runs.note: Add time only if the previous long run felt easy. Never add more than about 10% to your longest run of the last month.

weeks.advance: This week repeats. Keep it until a 5K under 35 min feels comfortable, then hold or set a new goal.
